claim_verbatim: "The experiments revealed that the P-CSEM model achieved a mAP of 59.52%, while that of the base model achieved a mAP of 58.57%. Although these models were not able to achieve comparable mAP results as in the Chole80 dataset, their results were deemed acceptable considering the differences in tool shape and design." (Discussion)
setting: EndoVis 2019 challenge frames, with frames containing non-Cholec80 tool classes removed
contrast: Cholec80 test (videos 41-80) mAP 93.14% vs EndoVis 2019 mAP 59.52%
D1_quote: "This evaluation was performed in order to observe the generalizability of the trained model on data from a different source." (Section 4, Discussion)
D2_quote: "The EndoVis 2019 challenge dataset was used for the generalizability evaluation." (Section 3.1)
D3_quote: "The Cholec80 dataset is available ... from the respected publisher upon request." (Data Availability Statement); external frames selected by rule: "these classes and, consequently, the image frames, were removed from processing." (Section 3.1)
D5_quote: "the mean of the average precision (mAP) of each of the tools was determined across the testing set." (Methods)
D7_quote: "Although these models were not able to achieve comparable mAP results as in the Chole80 dataset," (Section 4, Discussion); internal mAP 93.14% in Table 2
D8_quote: "This evaluation was performed in order to observe the generalizability of the trained model on data from a different source." (Section 4, Discussion)
supportable_claim: A Cholec80-trained P-CSEM model, applied to EndoVis 2019 frames limited to shared tool classes, reached mAP 59.52% (base 58.57%) against 93.14% internally. This is a large drop. The external centre, external frame and class counts, and external reference were not reported.
notes: The abstract makes no external claim, so the claim is taken from the Discussion. Rule: a different public dataset asserted as 'a different source' without naming another centre was rated p for D1 and D2. Rule: a public external dataset with a stated selection rule but no frame list and no code was rated p for D3. D8 was rated p because the report implies the same trained model was used but never states there was no re-training or fine-tuning. Although the title says 'detection', the task evaluated is frame-level presence classification.

claim_verbatim: "Our findings indicate that domain-specific pretraining with EndoViT yields notable advantages in complex downstream tasks. In the case of action triplet recognition, our approach outperforms ImageNet pretraining. In semantic segmentation, we surpass the state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance." (Abstract)
behaviour: Downstream semantic segmentation (mIoU), action triplet recognition (mAP) and phase recognition (accuracy), each after fine-tuning
setting: CholecSeg8k, CholecT45 (fold 5) and Cholec80: all derived from Cholec80 (one centre), which is also part of the Endo700k pretraining corpus
D1_quote: "To eliminate any potential data leakage, we exclude any images that appear in their validation or test sets from the pretraining dataset." (Dataset Preparation)
D2_quote: "Cholec80 and its subvariants CholecT45 and CholecSeg8k are additionally used for downstream tasks of surgical phase recognition, action triplet recognition, and semantic segmentation" (Table 1 caption)
D3_quote: "We release both our code and pretrained models to facilitate further research in this direction: https://github.com/DominikBatic/EndoViT." (Abstract); "we evaluate only on fold 5 as defined by [20]." (Methods)
D5_quote: "The reported metric is Accuracy averaged over all testing videos." (Phase recognition, Experiments)
D8_quote: "We replace the encoder of DPT with our ViT encoder but otherwise keep the training setup the same." (Semantic segmentation, Experiments)
supportable_claim: After fine-tuning on Cholec80-derived training data, EndoViT beat ImageNet pretraining on CholecT45 triplet mAP (fold 5 only) and gave the highest mIoU on CholecSeg8k. These are single-source benchmark results, not an external validation, and leakage from pretraining was controlled at the image level only, not the video level.
notes: The paper makes no external-validation claim. The 'external' sets are Cholec80 derivatives (same centre) that also contribute to pretraining. Leakage control excludes test and validation images only, so other frames of the same Cholec80 videos may stay in Endo700k (D1 p). Rule: D8 was rated n when the evaluated data were used for downstream training or fine-tuning, even though no internal-vs-external contrast is made; x was kept for D7 only. Splits are given by reference to published definitions, which was accepted as a manifest for D3.

claim_verbatim: "Through ablations, we demonstrate that domain-specific pretraining is particularly beneficial for more complex downstream tasks, such as Action Triplet Detection, and less effective and even unnecessary for simpler tasks, such as Surgical Phase Recognition." (Abstract)
behaviour: Action triplet detection (mAP) and surgical phase recognition (accuracy), each after fine-tuning
setting: CholecT45 (fold 5) and Cholec80: one centre; both also part of the Endo700k pretraining corpus
D1_quote: "To eliminate any potential data leakage, we do not include any images that appear in their validation or test sets." (Section 2.1)
D2_quote: "First, testing only on one fold allows us to have CholecT45 images in the pretraining." (Section 2.3)
D3_quote: "We will release both our code and pretrained models upon acceptance to facilitate further research in this direction." (Abstract)
D5_quote: "The reported metric is Phase Accuracy averaged over all testing videos." (Section 3)
D8_quote: "we replace the Resnet50 backbone with a ViT model and otherwise stick to the training and evaluation setup of TeCNO." (Section 2.3)
supportable_claim: On single-centre Cholec80 and CholecT45 benchmarks, after fine-tuning, Endo700k pretraining improved CholecT45 triplet mAP (fold 5) over ImageNet pretraining, but not Cholec80 phase accuracy. Two tasks are too few to support the general complexity-dependent claim, and this is not an external validation.
notes: This is a preprint of S02 (earlier version). Code was only promised 'upon acceptance' at the time, so D3 is p (splits by reference only). The same D8 rule as S02 applies. The arXiv page was accessed via ar5iv; the tables were not rendered in the retrieved text.

claim_verbatim: We also evaluated the generalizability of our method to similar tasks using two public datasets. The results demonstrate that our approach outperforms the current state-of-the-art (SOTA) self-supervised representation learning methods in various surgical image segmentation tasks.
behaviour: Multi-class segmentation (instrument type/part on EndoVisSub2017-RIS; tissue and instrument on CholecSeg8k) after SurgNet pretraining; mIoU and mDice, compared with other SSL and non-pretrained methods
unit: Dataset (public external datasets); within each, the fine-tuning/test split (sequence-level for EndoVis2017, unstated for CholecSeg8k)
setting: EndoVisSub2017-RIS (porcine da Vinci Xi; test sequences 9-10) and CholecSeg8k (Cholec80 subset), each after fine-tuning on its own training split; pretraining on IVIS-U (authors' robotic HPB videos)
contrast: Implied development (IVIS) to other datasets via "generalizability"; explicit contrast is between methods, not internal vs external
D1_quote: "use 2,400 images of eight sequences (#1-8) for fine-tuning and 600 images of two sequences (#9-10) for testing [...] perform 8-class segmentation on CholecSeg8k using 7,040 images for fine-tuning and 1,040 images for testing" (Sec. V.A)
D2_quote: "EndoVisSub2017-RIS dataset consists of 3,000 surgical video frames of stereo camera acquired in a da Vinci Xi robot during [...] CholecSeg8k dataset is a subset of the endoscopic images of Cholec80 provided by CAMMA" (Sec. V.A)
D3_quote: "The inference code and the pretrained model of our SurgNet, as well as the End User License Agreement (EULA) for applying our IVIS surgical image dataset can be found at: https://github.com/HanHuCAS/SurgNet" (Sec. I, footnote 1)
D4_quote: "We follow the 6-class instrument type segmentation and 3-class instrument part segmentation protocols in [75], and use 2,400 images of eight sequences (#1-8) for fine-tuning and 600 images of two sequences (#9-10) for testing" (Sec. V.A; Tables IV-V give mIoU/mDice only)
D5_quote: "use mIoU and mDice for multi-class segmentation tasks" (Sec. V.A)
D6_quote: "The dataset is annotated with 7 types of surgical instruments" (Sec. V.A)
D7_quote: "Both our method and UM-MAE achieve nearly 80% mIoU and 90% Dice" (Sec. V.C, Table III (IVIS-E))
D8_quote: "We follow [77] and perform 8-class segmentation on CholecSeg8k using 7,040 images for fine-tuning and 1,040 images for testing [...] use 2,400 images of eight sequences (#1-8) for fine-tuning" (Sec. V.A)
supportable_claim: After fine-tuning on each public dataset's own training split, a SurgNet-pretrained UPerNet reached mIoU 0.63/0.81 (instrument type/part) on EndoVisSub2017 sequences 9-10 and mIoU 0.71 on the CholecSeg8k test images, above UM-MAE and baselines partly copied from other papers. This supports benefit of the pretrained representation for target-domain fine-tuning, not generalisation of a fixed model to new data; no CIs, single split.
notes: Linked repository inspected (git clone of github.com/HanHuCAS/SurgNet): provides fine-tuning/test code, pretrained weights, an EndoVisSub2017 config and fine-tuned EndoVis2017 weights, so the EndoVis2017 evaluation is replayable from public data plus the sequence split; no CholecSeg8k config or split file (split only "follow [77]"), hence D3 p. Claim spans two datasets whose evidence differs -> p for D1-D3. CholecSeg8k split unit not stated; frame-level split of consecutive frames would leak near-duplicates between fine-tune and test (not shown, so not rated n). No zero-shot external estimate at any point, so D8 n. Baselines in Tables IV-V are taken from [75]/[77] (different implementations/splits), limiting the "outperforms SOTA" contrast. Per-class external support not given for 6- and 8-class mIoU (EndoVis2017 test sequences may lack some instrument types). D7 rated because "generalizability" implies a development-to-other-dataset contrast; internal IVIS-E performance on the same metric is reported. Quotes verified after NFKC/whitespace normalisation and joining of "2, 400"-style thousands separators in the extracted text.

Frame counts are internally inconsistent (EndoVis 17 is called 600 images but described as 10 x 300 frames; the DVR frame formula does not match the stated video durations). D5 was rated on the metric only; the missing external estimate is reflected in the supportable claim. The data availability links are generic (a Roboflow page and a PMC figure) and there is no code.

claim_verbatim: "Focusing on the application of PAWSS to surgical scenes, we evaluate on MICCAI 2015 challenge instrument tracking challenge and in vivo datasets, showing that our approach performs the best among all submitted methods and also has promising performance on in vivo surgical instrument tracking." (Abstract)
behaviour: Single-target instrument tracking; centre-point distance error and accuracy at 20/30-pixel thresholds
setting: EndoVis 2015 (MICCAI) robotic ex vivo and conventional in vivo test sets, scored by the challenge organisers; further in vivo sequences of unstated source

D3_quote: "Our algorithm is publicly available online" (github.com/surgical-vision/PAWSS); "The dataset has not released ground truth for test data." (EndoVis experiments)
D4_quote: "We have summarized the frame number for each sequence and have shown the accuracy evaluation separately" (EndoVis experiments, Table 6; training sequences only)
D5_quote: "We also test on some other in vivo sequences and show the result in Fig. 18." (In vivo surgical instrument experiments)
D6_quote: "The dataset has not released ground truth for test data." (EndoVis experiments)
D8_quote: "To illustrate the generalization of our proposed framework, we use the same parameter setting through all experiments." (Experiments, Table 1)
supportable_claim: On the EndoVis 2015 tracking challenge test sets, the official report gave PAWSS, run with fixed parameters and no offline training, the lowest mean distance error among the few submitted methods (29.66 px for the robotic tracked point). The authors' own EndoVis numbers use training sequences that they re-annotated; the test results come from the organisers' report, whose reference is not released. D6 was rated p rather than a because the in vivo sequences have no reference at all. The centre of the EndoVis data is not stated in the text.

claim_verbatim: "The obtained results show that using solely procedure-specific data can lead to substantial improvements of 13.8%, 9.5%, and 36.8% compared to ImageNet pretraining. However, extending this data with more heterogeneous surgical data further increases performance by an additional 5.0%, 5.2%, and 2.5%, suggesting that increasing diversity within SSL data is beneficial for model performance." (Abstract)

D2_quote: "It should be noted that all videos of patients included in the test set are excluded from SurgeNet." (Methods)

The paper reports no evaluation at an external centre.

The stated claim is about pretraining benefit, which the evidence supports. Patient-level exclusion of test videos from pretraining was accepted as a source-level control for D2. RAMIE and RARP are private (D3 p). Per-class counts are not given. CholecSeg8k annotation is described only as 'annotated with semantic segmentation masks'. The Figure 1 caption ties the results to five-fold cross-validation, which may mean the results are not from the held-out test set.

claim_verbatim: AI has potential to detect unsafe dissection and prevent BDIs through real-time intraoperative decision-support.
behaviour: Detection of unsafe dissection: proportion of tool-tissue interactions outside GoNoGoNet's Go zone (BDI vs control videos, % difference with 99% CI) and zone of the injury-causing interaction
unit: Video/procedure (11 BDI and 11 control laparoscopic cholecystectomy videos)
setting: Retrospectively procured LC videos with documented BDI (authors' collaborator network and open-access sources) and controls from a 333-video bank; stated not used in training
contrast: None internal vs external; contrast is BDI vs control group (and threshold levels)
D1_quote: "None of the videos from either group had been used in the training of the model previously." (Methods, Dataset)
D2_quote: "procured from the authors’ network of collaborators as well as from open access sources [...] None of the videos from either group had been used in the training of the model previously." (Methods, Dataset)
D4_quote: "A total of 126:45 min of tool-tissue interactions (BDI group = 70:01 min; Control group = 56:44 min) were analyzed" (Results; Table 2 gives percentages without interaction counts)
D5_quote: "LC videos with BDIs had a significantly greater proportion of sharp, blunt, or any dissection occurring outside of the Go zone compared to LC videos in the Control group (p < 0.01)." (Results)
D6_quote: "only included if all tool-tissue interactions were deemed to have occurred within the surgeon-assessed Go zone [...] compared to AI-annotated Go and No-Go zones on an initial reference frame within the same minute of each video" (Methods, Dataset)
supportable_claim: In 11 BDI videos and 11 expert-selected "safe" LC videos not used in training, a larger share of tool-tissue interactions in BDI videos fell outside GoNoGoNet's Go zone (zones read from one reference frame per minute). At the default output 6/11 injury-causing interactions lay inside the Go zone; this fell to 2/11 only after the Go threshold was raised post hoc on the same videos. Accuracy of detecting unsafe dissection and any effect on BDI prevention were not measured.
notes: Decision rule: D7/D8 rated x literally because the report does not compare development and external settings. Flag for consensus: the abstract result is reported "after maximizing the probability threshold" (80%), chosen by modulating the threshold on the evaluation BDI videos themselves; were D8 applicable it would be n. Controls were selected conditional on all interactions lying within the surgeon-assessed Go zone, which builds in part of the BDI-control difference. Interaction counts, the person(s) labelling interactions and inter-rater agreement are not reported. Model is the U-Net version of GoNoGoNet (not the PSPNet version validated in S10). No code or data availability statement.

claim_verbatim: AI can be used to identify safe and dangerous zones of dissection within the surgical field, with high specificity/PPV for Go zones and high sensitivity/NPV for No-Go zones.
behaviour: Semantic segmentation of Go and No-Go zones; F1/Dice and IoU (primary), pixel accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV against expert consensus
unit: Frame (47 frames) from 25 LC videos; generalisation to new videos, surgeons and institutions and to an external expert panel
setting: 25 prospectively collected LC videos (5 countries, 9 surgeons, 7 institutions) annotated by 6 SAGES Safe Cholecystectomy Task Force experts not involved in training
contrast: None in the claim; Discussion relates the results to the model's prior development results
D1_quote: "There were no duplicate videos and none were previously used in the original training dataset." (Results)
D2_quote: "Videos were obtained from 5 countries (Canada, USA, France, Bolivia and Thailand), 9 surgeons and 7 institutions. There were no duplicate videos and none were previously used in the original training dataset." (Results)
D4_quote: "A total of 47 frames were extracted for validation." (Results)
D5_quote: "Identification of Go and No-Go zones by GoNoGoNet was compared to expert-derived consensus using mean F1 Dice Score, and pixel accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV) and negative predictive value (NPV)." (Abstract, Methods)
D6_quote: "A total of 47 frames from 25 LC videos, procured from 3 countries and 9 surgeons, were annotated simultaneously by an expert panel of 6 surgeons and GoNoGoNet." (Abstract, Results; protocol in Methods, Annotations)
D7_quote: "Nevertheless, algorithmic performance seemed to replicate prior preliminary results [6]." (Discussion)
D8_quote: "A Convolutional DNN was previously trained to perform semantic segmentation (i.e. delineate the boundary) of the Go and No-Go zones of dissection during videos of LC [6]." (Methods, AI model)
supportable_claim: Against a >50% pixel-agreement consensus of 6 external experts on 47 frames from 25 new LC videos (7 institutions), the previously trained GoNoGoNet reached mean Dice 0.80 for No-Go and 0.58 for Go zones (Go sensitivity 0.52, PPV 0.70). Estimates vary strongly with the consensus definition (the >50% definition was singled out after viewing all three), have no CIs, and apply only to frames pre-selected for full view of the hepatocystic triangle.
notes: D7 rated (not x) because the Discussion interprets the external result as replicating development results without reporting them here. D8 p: the model is described as previously trained, but no explicit statement that weights and output thresholds were unchanged for this evaluation. D2 p: no-duplicate assertion without a described check; institutions not stated to be absent from the 136 training institutions. Inconsistencies: abstract "3 countries" vs Results "5 countries"; Table 2 threshold labelled "49" vs ">50%" in text. Six of 31 videos excluded (top-down approach or inadequate view). "High PPV" for Go zones rests on 0.70 (SD 0.21). No code or data availability statement.

behaviour: Frame-level CVS assessment (3 criteria + overall); balanced accuracy
unit: video (evaluation videos from the Cholec80/m2cai16-workflow pool)

D1_quote: "We use the 17 videos from the CholecSeg8K dataset as the development set and the remaining 100 as the evaluation set." (Section IV-A)
D2_quote: "The combined Cholec80 [31]and m2cai16-workflow [32] dataset consists of 117 videos after excluding duplicate cases [24]." (Section IV-A)

supportable_claim: On 6,000 frames from 100 held-out videos of the same Cholec80/m2cai16-workflow source (not another centre), a rule-based CVS assessment built on segmentation models had higher balanced accuracy than a re-implemented DeepCVS (overall 0.54 vs 0.49); per-class counts and replay manifest not reported.
notes: Report itself makes no other-centre claim; 'external' (review label) corresponds to same-source held-out videos. Segmentation trained on CholecSeg170/CholecSeg8K (derived from Cholec80); CVS rule-based, no classifier trained on CVS6K. DeepCVS re-implementation training details unclear. Quotations taken from the arXiv PDF/ar5iv; verify wording against PDF at consensus. Rule A1: D7 = x when neither claim nor report contrasts internal vs external; D8 still rated.

claim_verbatim: SurgSmart is not only capable of accurately detecting and positioning anatomic regions in LC but also has better performance than that of the trainees and seniors in terms of individual still images and the whole set.

Rated D1 n on the explicit random image-level assignment; D2 p because other-source origin is asserted without record. Authors state model 'may not be fully generalizable to other hospitals'. claim_verbatim: AOMA achieves state-of-the-art results on two practical scenarios: (1) general videos to surgical videos, (2) public surgical videos to in-house surgical videos, while reducing the test runtime substantially.
behaviour: One-shot binary instrument segmentation from robotic surgical video; IoU and Dice (per-video, averaged), compared with other one-shot methods; rated element is scenario (1)
unit: Video/dataset: target videos from datasets not used in training (EndoVis17, 8 sequences; EndoVis18, 15 sequences)
setting: EndoVis17 and EndoVis18 (porcine in-vivo, da Vinci) after meta-training on Davis16 + EndoVis15 ex-vivo; first-frame mask of each target video supplied at test time
contrast: Between methods within the target domain; source-to-target domain shift implied (no source performance reported)
D1_quote: "Davis16 (50 videos) + EndoVis15 (4 videos) [...] EndoVis17 (8 videos), EndoVis18 (15 videos)" (Table 1)
D2_quote: "4 × 110-frame ex-vivo sequences (EndoVis15) (Speidel et al., 2015) are added into the source domain" (Sec. 4.1)
D3_quote: "EndoVis17 (Allan et al., 2019) is a public challenge dataset from 2017 MICCAI EndoVis Instrument Segmentation." (Sec. 4.1)
D4_quote: "It releases 8 × 225-frame in-vivo surgical video sequences [...] Each sequence includes 149 frames" (Sec. 4.1)
D5_quote: "We employ the mean intersection-over-union (IoU) and Dice coefficient (Dice) to quantitatively analyze the results" (Sec. 4.2)
D6_quote: "We only use the classes regarding surgical instruments in this work." (Sec. 4.1 (EndoVis18))
D7_quote: "Normally training the model (Base) on general videos cannot generalize well on surgical videos." (Sec. 4.4)
D8_quote: "Note that we provide the first frame mask for each testing surgical video. [...] In Fig. 8, we investigate the effect of the key hyper-parameters on our online adaptation strategy [...] We report segmentation results on EndoVis17" (Sec. 4.1; Sec. 4.7)
supportable_claim: With one labelled first frame per target video plus test-time online adaptation, and adaptation hyper-parameters examined on EndoVis17, AOMA meta-trained on Davis16 + EndoVis15 reached mean IoU 77.1% on EndoVis17 and 68.4% on EndoVis18, above re-implemented one-shot baselines (averages of 5 trials, no CIs). Without any target adaptation the base model reached 60.5%/47.2% IoU. Source-domain performance is not reported.
notes: Claim lists two scenarios; per protocol the first (General -> Surgical) is rated. Scenario (2) (EndoVis17/18 -> HKPWH, 4 x 100-frame prostatectomy sequences from Prince of Wales Hospital) would be rated similarly except D2 (other centre, likely m); no availability statement for HKPWH. Decision rule: the D8 zero-shot exception applies only when the zero-shot estimate is of the model/procedure the claim is about; the Base (no adaptation) rows are separated but estimate a different procedure, and AOMA itself uses external labels (first frame) and test-time updates, with hyper-parameters (gamma, sigma) studied on the target EndoVis17 data, so D8 n. D3 p: target data are whole public releases (manifest) but no code statement. Reference masks taken from challenge releases without describing annotation (D6 p). Quotes verified after NFKC normalisation (ligatures in extracted text).

claim_verbatim: The validation experiment showed that LSQS could help non‐expert users to more easily achieve expert‐level control of the laparoscope.
behaviour: Laparoscope control: proportion of extracted frames whose LSQS-computed Occupation Rate falls in the "excellent" range, with vs without LSQS (chi-square)
unit: Procedure (12 laparoscopic partial nephrectomies, 3 per user-condition), analysed at image level
setting: Prospective live use of the deployed system (PaddleSeg DeepLabv3+ on EdgeBoard) in urology at Renmin Hospital of Wuhan University, the development centre; procedure type absent from training data
contrast: With vs without LSQS and non-expert vs expert; no internal-vs-external comparison
D1_quote: "including radical prostatectomy, partial adrenal resection, and radical bladder cancer resection [...] verification experiment involving 12 laparoscopic partial nephrectomies from patients with renal" (Sec. 2.1; Sec. 2.5)
D2_quote: "Non‐expert laparoscopy user used LSQS to control the laparoscopic lens in three procedures" (Sec. 2.5)
D3_quote: "Data can be obtained from corresponding authors upon reasonable request." (Data availability statement)
D4_quote: "300 images (after excluding fuzzy/unclear images) were extracted [...] Non‐expert without LSQS 50.78% (457/900)" (Sec. 2.5; Table 4)
D5_quote: "were extracted to calculate the corresponding OR and the number of images within an appropriate level." (Sec. 2.5)
D6_quote: "Finally, we predicted the classified pictures through the trained segmentation model and outputted the OR range, in order to determine the corresponding threshold based on the result." (Sec. 2.4)
supportable_claim: In 12 partial nephrectomies at the development centre (one non-expert and one expert operator, 3 procedures per condition), the share of extracted frames that LSQS itself classified as "excellent" rose from 50.78% to 81.67% for the non-expert when LSQS was used. There is no independent reference for laparoscope control, frames are clustered within 3 procedures per arm and one operator per group, and segmentation accuracy on these procedures was not assessed.
notes: Only validation claim in the abstract; the basis of the external classification by Carstens et al. is unclear (training pool mixes 20 Renmin videos with Cholec80 videos; internal validation is a random image-level split). D7/D8 rated x literally (no development-vs-external comparison); if applicable, D8 would be m-like (model deployed unchanged; OR thresholds set on 20 separate videos). Decision rules: procedures performed prospectively with the deployed frozen system count as a source-level control for D2 (m) although same centre; data "on reasonable request" with no code or manifest = D3 n. D4 p: Table 4 denominators (900 per arm) conflict with "300 images" extracted. D5/D6 n: the endpoint is the system's own output classified by thresholds derived from model outputs; no human reference on the experiment frames. Deployed model (PaddleSeg DeepLabv3+) differs from the PSPNet reported in the abstract. Text extraction is two-column interleaved; Sec. 2-4 quotes verified against a column-aware re-extraction of the PDF (pdfplumber), claim against the supplied text.
